title: Now & Next Board
strapline: Just two pictures — the thing you're doing and the thing that comes after — so the next step never ambushes anyone.
intent: Children who are overwhelmed by a whole timetable get the world shrunk to two manageable steps.
Children learn that a less-preferred task ('tidy up') is followed by a preferred one ('garden') — motivation you can see.
Children practise finishing one thing and moving to the next without a meltdown at the join.
Children build trust that adults keep their word: the 'next' picture really does happen.
Children gain a shared, wordless way to negotiate transitions when talk is too much in the moment.
implementation: Keep it genuinely to two frames — 'now' and 'next' — velcro or magnet so cards swap fast in the moment.
Photograph the child's actual activities so the picture matches their reality, not a generic symbol.
Sequence a preferred activity into the 'next' slot after something harder, and honour it every single time.
Show and say it together — 'now we wash hands, next we have snack' — then hand the card over as the step completes.
Let the child post the 'now' card into a finished pocket when done — a small ritual that marks the transition.
Fade it gradually for children who no longer need it, but keep one to hand for hard days and big changes.
key_questions: What's the picture that comes next?
Shall we post the finished card away?
You did the tricky bit — what did we say came after?
Which picture would you like in the 'next' spot?

impact.text: Children move from one activity to the next with support and less distress.
Children begin to wait and delay a preferred thing, sometimes gracefully, when they can see it coming.
Children follow simple two-step sequences shown in pictures and words.
Children regulate a big feeling at a transition using the board as a shared anchor.
Children show growing independence — checking the board and moving on without being told twice.

enhancements: A travelling lanyard version for a child who needs the same support in the garden, the hall and on outings.
A choice board feeding the 'next' slot — the child picks their reward activity from two options.
A 'first/then' spoken script paired with the pictures so staff use identical language every time.
A photo of a trusted adult on the 'next' card for separation moments ('now play, next Mummy comes').

playing_exploring: Children handle and post the cards, making the tool physical and playful rather than imposed.
Choosing the 'next' picture gives children agency in how their moment unfolds.
active_learning: Seeing a reward coming keeps children going through the less fun bit.
Completing the swap themselves builds a felt sense of 'I can manage this change.'
creating_thinking: Children grasp simple cause and consequence — finish this, then that happens.
They start to predict and plan two steps ahead rather than living only in the now.
